samples.identification: Minimal Python COM TypeLib scriptlet hijack
samples.reason: At module load, winreg.SetValue writes the HKCU Software\Classes\TypeLib\{00020430-0000-0000-C000-000000000046}\2.0\0\win64 default value to script:C:\ProgramData\agent.sct. This redirects a system TypeLib reference to a scriptlet and supports attempted COM activation hijacking. The browser CLSID variable is unused. The WScript.Shell cmd.exe /c stage.cmd scriptlet is stored only in a Python string; the sample neither writes it nor calls it. No activation, privilege elevation, payload theft, or family identity is claimed. A research/authorized-lab use is possible, but no such context accompanies this standalone registry takeover.
samples.marker_line: TypeLib hijack: redirects COM activation to a scriptlet; bind writes
samples.coverage_goal: One distinct hostile result is supported: COM TypeLib persistence. Traced the registry sink and embedded stage. Added SetValue/SetValueEx destination-value linkage. The shell command is unexecuted literal text, and there is no stage write, encoding, hidden-window option, elevated boundary crossing, or collection/send chain to support 3-5 independent hostile traits. This is an evidence limit, not a missing matcher for a demonstrated effect.
